note: Crafts of the emotional_logical axis — a horizon Reach now brought online. Pathos is the emotional-pole tradition (feeling as force, resonance-of-heart); Logos the logical-pole (reason as force, inference-as-power). Learned by traveling the Reach or training with the Deepfeelers / the Reasoners. Both drift the wielder toward their pole. Function tags included per canon. axes signed for engine compat. Authored by Aevi (PO), SNG-016 — first horizon-axis tradition.

abilities.name: Pathos
abilities.narrationHints: Feeling made a force — the true emotion of a room surfaced, a grief shared and eased, a passion kindled or cooled by one who feels it first and hardest.
abilities.description: Feel the true emotion under a room or a person past what they show, share a feeling so it eases, and kindle a genuine passion in the willing. The emotional-pole mastery — not manipulation, resonance.
abilities.notFor: Forcing a feeling on the unwilling (Pathos resonates, it does not compel); cold analysis (that's Logos); faking an emotion — Pathos works by feeling it truly first.

tree.name: Open Heart
tree.grants: Feel the true emotion under a room or a person, past what they show; share a feeling so it eases (a grief halved, a fear steadied); kindle a genuine passion in the willing.
tree.cannot: Reads and shares; does not command; the guarded can close to it; feeling their pain means feeling it.

tree.name: Shared Fire
tree.grants: Move a crowd by feeling-with-them; carry a person through an emotion too big to bear alone; make an unspoken feeling undeniable in the open.
tree.cannot: You take on what you move — the cost is real; a will set against feeling resists; moving a mob is riding a wave, not steering it.

tree.name: Deep Chord
tree.grants: Feeling at the scale of peoples — turn a room, a mob, a mourning-crowd by the truth of shared feeling; reach a heart no reason could; hold another's whole emotional weight for a time. The Deepfeelers' power in miniature.
tree.cannot: The wielder drifts emotion-hot — feeling everything, all the time, until the self drowns; emotion without reason to shape it becomes storm, and a storm forecloses on thought as surely as ice does on feeling.

abilities.name: Turning Word
abilities.narrationHints: The room turns — a crowd, a court, a mob — moved as one by the exact true thing said the exact right way.
abilities.description: The social capstone: move a whole gathering at once — turn a hostile crowd, sway a council, stop a mob — by finding and speaking the one thing that reaches all of them. Pathos and Logos fused into mass persuasion.
abilities.notFor: Individual mind-control; moving those with no shared feeling or reason; forcing against a set will.

tree.name: Turning Word
tree.grants: Turn a crowd or council decisively — the room moves as one when you find the word that reaches them.
tree.cannot: Needs a real shared chord to strike; a crowd set immovably resists; you feel/carry what you move.

tree.name: Word That Holds
tree.grants: The turning holds past the moment — a crowd moved stays moved after you have gone, a council's decision keeps its shape when you are not in the room. And where there is no shared chord to strike, you can make one: name the thing they did not know they held in common. A room turned off something ugly does not merely stop: the turning closes the rift that was opening in it, and people who were a minute from being enemies go back to being neighbours.
tree.cannot: A chord you made is a chord you are answerable for; the Rhetors hold that inventing a commonality is how peoples are built and also how they are ruined. It still cannot move a will genuinely set. And you carry what you move for as long as it stays moved.

abilities.plainly: A social action, and it needs two poles: threnodist and syllogist together. You turn an entire crowd or council at once by finding the one thing they all already feel and saying it. It needs a real shared chord to strike — a crowd with nothing in common cannot be turned, and the craft fails outright rather than working weakly. And you are answerable for what you struck: a room you turned toward something will hold you responsible for where it goes, which is a debt that outlasts the scene.

abilities.name: Inescapable Conclusion
abilities.narrationHints: You lay the premises down one at a time, each one they must agree to, until they arrive — of their own reasoning — at a conclusion they would have run from if they'd seen it coming.
abilities.description: Lay premises down one at a time, each one they must agree to, until they arrive by their own reasoning at a conclusion they would have fled. The Syllogist art of the inescapable argument — and the trap is that it is TRUE.
abilities.notFor: It binds only the reasonable — a mind that will simply refuse a true conclusion cannot be caught by one. And a true argument binds you too; you cannot walk someone to a conclusion you are unwilling to stand on yourself.

tree.name: Inescapable Conclusion
tree.grants: Bind a reasoning mind to a conclusion by an argument it cannot honestly escape.
tree.cannot: It fails against those who refuse reason itself, it binds its wielder to the same truth, and a conclusion someone was walked into by force of logic can curdle into resentment of the one who walked them.

tree.name: Standing Proof
tree.grants: Walk a whole body of reasoning minds to the same conclusion at once — a council, a court, a school — and the binding holds against later private doubt, because each of them watched the others agree. The chain can be built across days now rather than one exchange.
tree.cannot: It still fails entirely against those who will simply refuse a true conclusion, and a group holds more of them than a person does. It binds you to the same truth, publicly and on the record. And a conclusion a body was walked into together curdles together — the Syllogists have begun more than one schism this way.

abilities.name: Shared Grief
abilities.narrationHints: You take up the lament and others find their own grief given shape in it — not lessened, but no longer carried alone, the weight spread across every voice that joins.
abilities.description: Lead a lament that spreads one grief across many, so no single heart carries the whole. The Threnodist art of the shared song, and the mourning-singers' first true gift.
abilities.notFor: It shares grief, it does not erase it — a sorrow sung together is still a sorrow. And the one who leads the lament carries the gathering-point; you hold the grief of all who join while you sing.

tree.name: Shared Grief
tree.grants: Lead a shared lament that spreads one grief across many, so none carries it alone.
tree.cannot: It cannot remove grief, only distribute its weight; the singer bears the gathering of it; and a grief shared is a grief made real to everyone who joins the song.

tree.name: Named Sorrow
tree.grants: The lament finds the true shape of what is mourned. Singing it, you perceive what the grief is ACTUALLY for — the loss beneath the stated one — and those who join hear it named as well, often for the first time.
tree.cannot: Naming is not mending; a sorrow correctly named can wound worse before it eases. The singer cannot choose what surfaces, and what the lament names in company cannot be unnamed.

tree.cannot: You hold the gathering while you hold the lament, and days of it mark the singer; handing the point on requires a singer able to take it; and a grief carried by everyone becomes part of what that place IS — the GM records it in the world, not the character.

abilities.name: Names of the Lost
abilities.narrationHints: You sing the names — all of them, every one lost — and for the length of the song they are not gone, exactly; they are HELD, present in the keeping of their names.
abilities.description: Sing the names of the lost — all of them — and for the length of the song they are held present rather than gone. The Threnodist naming-song, and the deep work of those who refuse to let go be the same as forget.
abilities.notFor: It holds the lost in memory, it does not return them — a name kept is not a life restored. And to sing all the names is to carry all the losses at once, for the length of the song and after.

tree.name: Names of the Lost
tree.grants: Sing the names of the lost, holding them present in memory for the length of the lament.
tree.cannot: It cannot restore the dead, only attend them; it lays every named loss on the singer at once; and the song ends, and they are gone again, and you chose to feel that twice.

tree.name: Kept Names
tree.grants: The names keep past the lament. Sung over a place — a barrow, a battlefield, a hall — the attending holds without you, and any who come after feel the lost attended there. The song can hold names you were told rather than only names you carried yourself. Those who hear the names are strengthened by the attending — steadied, clearer about what they are doing and why, and harder to move off it.
tree.cannot: It still does not return them; a name kept is not a life restored. A place that holds its lost is a place that does not move on, which is not always mercy. And a name taken from another's telling is held on trust — sing one wrong and the Threnodists count it a wound.

abilities.description: The Threnodist capstone — the complete lament, all grief given full voice at once, that lets those who hear it finally finish a mourning they could not finish alone. The greatest and costliest gift of the singers: to be grieved completely is to be freed.

abilities.name: Grief That Stops
abilities.narrationHints: They set it down inside them the way you would set down a stone. The heart is not built to carry that.
abilities.description: ⚠️ THE HEART-TUNERS' CRAFT. Pathos SHARES a feeling; this INSTALLS one at a weight no body holds. Not sorrow — sorrow's full weight, all at once, without the years that usually come with it. Some hearts stop. Most do not, and those people are changed.
abilities.notFor: A heart with nothing to grieve — it uses THEIR losses, not invented ones, so someone who has lost nothing is nearly immune. And it CANNOT BE AIMED at an outcome: you set the weight down, the body decides.

tree.name: Grief That Stops
tree.grants: Set the full weight of their own losses on them at once. They are overwhelmed and afterward not the same.
tree.cannot: Inventing a grief. Anyone who has lost nothing.

tree.name: All Of It
tree.grants: Set every loss down together with nothing held back. A heart sometimes stops. You will not know beforehand which.
tree.cannot: Knowing beforehand. Taking it back once set.

mechanic.note: ⚠️ A HOBBLE WITH A LETHAL TAIL — the kill is a possibility, never a roll you aim. Resolve r2 as incapacitation plus a small independent chance of a stopped heart, weighted by how much the target has actually lost. NOT a FIGHT craft: it does not fight.

abilities.plainly: A social contest against the target's composure, drawing only on losses they have actually suffered — a target who has lost nothing gets a large bonus to resist. On a win they are incapacitated for several minutes and carry a lasting penalty to composure rolls afterward. At rank 2 the GM additionally rolls a small independent chance that the target's heart stops, scaled to how much they have genuinely lost. You cannot aim for that outcome and you cannot call it off once cast.

abilities.name: Closing Argument
abilities.narrationHints: Every step is one they agreed to. That is what makes the last step impossible to refuse.
abilities.description: ⚠️ THE CORNERS' CRAFT. A Syllogist walks a person, honestly, from premises they already hold to a conclusion that ends them — that the work was worthless, that they cannot be forgiven, that the only consistent act remaining is the one they will now perform. NOTHING IN IT IS FALSE. That is the whole horror.
abilities.notFor: Anyone who will not reason — the unreasonable are genuinely immune and the Corners resent it. And it CANNOT USE A FALSE PREMISE: the argument must be sound or it does nothing at all.

tree.name: Closing Argument
tree.grants: Walk them, honestly, to a conclusion that unmakes their footing. They cannot act against it while it holds.
tree.cannot: A false premise. Anyone who refuses to follow.

tree.name: Only Consistent Act
tree.grants: Reach the conclusion where the consistent act is a final one — and STOP TALKING. What they do next is theirs.
tree.cannot: Making them. It is their hand and both of you know it.

mechanic.note: ⚠️ THE ONLY KILL IN THE CATALOG THE WIELDER DOES NOT PERFORM. Resolve as a hobble; the lethal outcome is the target's OWN act, gated on the argument being sound and the target being a reasoner. The engine should never render it as damage dealt.

abilities.plainly: A social contest against the target's resolve. You must be able to state a sound argument from something they already believe — the GM judges soundness, and an unsound argument fails automatically. On a win they cannot act against that conclusion for the rest of the scene. At rank 2, if the conclusion is that a final act is the only consistent one, the GM decides whether the target performs it; you never roll for that part. The target may disengage from the conversation at any time, and anyone who refuses to reason is immune outright.

abilities.name: Keening
abilities.narrationHints: A grief-cry pitched past speech — not loud so much as TRUE, and the truth of it buckles the knees of everyone in earshot. Heard, never aimed.
abilities.description: Release a grief you actually hold as sound, and everyone in earshot who can feel is staggered — weapons lowered, a charge broken, a pursuit stalled. It works through walls, and it lands on you too. The Threnodists' first offense: heard, never aimed.
abilities.notFor: A silent kill (it is heard, always); sparing your friends — ANYONE ELSE IN EARSHOT IS STRUCK ONE RUNG LOWER, and the wielder takes 'damaging' at rank 3; the deaf; anything that does not feel.

tree.name: Cry Let Go
tree.grants: Release a grief you actually hold as sound. Everyone in earshot who can feel is staggered — weapons lowered, a charge broken, a pursuit stalled for a breath. It works through walls and in the dark.
tree.cannot: It is UNAIMED — ANYONE ELSE IN EARSHOT IS STRUCK ONE RUNG LOWER, and the wielder takes the same one rung lower. The deaf are untouched. It needs a grief you truly carry; a performed one makes noise and nothing else.

tree.name: Held Note
tree.grants: Sustain it — the stagger holds while you keen, and those caught cannot rally. Or narrow it to one throat and drop them where they stand.
tree.cannot: Sustaining costs you the whole time; you cannot act while you hold it. The grief-hardened ride it out. Narrowing to one means the rest hear a woman weeping and come to see.

tree.name: Threnody
tree.grants: The full lament — a crowd, a hall, a street stopped where it stands and made to feel what you feel. Fights end. Some of the caught do not get up; grief at full weight stops hearts, and the Threnodists know it.
tree.cannot: You are emptied by it — what you spent, you no longer carry, and some of it does not come back. A tradition of grief-singers can answer it in kind.

abilities.name: Contradiction
abilities.narrationHints: You name the flaw in what someone is doing WHILE they are doing it, and the doing comes apart. Not a taunt — a demonstration. Spoken, precise, and only ever second.
abilities.description: Interrupt an action by naming its actual error out loud while it is happening — the plan with the gap, the boast with the hole, the ritual with the wrong step — and the move falters. The Syllogists' first offense, and the only one that cannot start a fight.
abilities.notFor: Opening an exchange (there must be a claim or an action to contradict); the mindless, the mid-swing berserk, anything not REASONING; being right — it works on the flaw, so a sound plan is immune.

tree.name: Named Flaw
tree.grants: Interrupt an action or claim by naming its actual error out loud — the plan with the gap, the boast with the hole, the ritual with the wrong step. The move falters and must be reworked — the interruption hinders them for as long as the flaw stands unanswered.
tree.cannot: REACTIVE ONLY — nothing to contradict means nothing happens. The flaw must be REAL; inventing one is Falsecraft and this is not that. The unreasoning are immune.

tree.name: Reductio
tree.grants: Follow their position to where it collapses. A commitment they made becomes a thing they cannot act on — the oath that now forbids the blow, the doctrine that now forbids the door.
tree.cannot: They must have STATED the position; you cannot bind someone to a belief they never claimed. The shameless simply proceed anyway.

tree.name: Collapse
tree.grants: Take a whole structure apart in front of the people who live in it — a case, a command, a faith. What they were doing stops, and it stays stopped.
tree.cannot: You have made a permanent enemy of everyone whose ground you took, and the truth of it will not soften that. A structure with no flaw stands, and you look like a fool.

intensity.conserve: a single objection — they lose the beat, no more
intensity.surge: take the whole structure; YOU HAVE MADE A PERMANENT ENEMY of everyone standing on it

abilities.name: Carried Name
abilities.narrationHints: You hold a dead person's name the way a room holds a struck bell. Speak it and what they were comes back into the space — not a ghost, a WEIGHT. People remember correctly for as long as you hold it.
abilities.description: Speak a name you carry and the room remembers that person as they WERE — not the softened version, not the useful one. Lies about the dead do not hold while you hold the name. The Threnodists' keeping-craft.
abilities.notFor: Raising, speaking with, or asking anything of the dead; a name you never learned; making anyone feel better about it.

tree.name: Name Held
tree.grants: Speak a name you carry and the room remembers that person as they WERE — not the softened version, not the useful version. Lies about the dead do not hold while you hold the name.
tree.cannot: You must have KNOWN them or been told truly. It corrects memory; it does not summon. And what returns is accurate, which is sometimes worse for everyone present.

tree.name: Kept Room
tree.grants: Hold several, or hold one long enough that a place keeps them — a threshold, a stone, a hall that will not let the name go crooked.
tree.cannot: Holding costs, and the names you carry do not leave you between uses. A Threnodist knows exactly how many they hold.

tree.name: Whole Lament
tree.grants: Everyone a place has lost, held at once, correctly. Communities have changed their minds about their own history under this.
tree.cannot: You are carrying all of it while you hold it. And an honest accounting of a place's dead will name people that place decided to forget on purpose.

abilities.name: Shared Weight
abilities.narrationHints: You take part of what someone is carrying and carry it yourself. Not comfort — TRANSFER. They can stand up because some of it is on you now.
abilities.description: Take a share of another's grief, fear or despair onto yourself, and they function again — steady hands, clear speech, able to act. Not comfort, TRANSFER. The Threnodists' mercy, and a real one because it is not free.
abilities.notFor: Removing grief (it MOVES, it does not vanish); putting it down again quickly; taking what someone will not give; physical wounds.

tree.name: Portion Taken
tree.grants: Take a share of another's grief, fear, or despair onto yourself. They function again — steady hands, clear speech, able to act. You carry it in their place.
tree.cannot: They must GIVE it; taking uninvited fails and they will know you tried. And you now have it. It does not evaporate because the crisis passed.

tree.name: Steady Hand
tree.grants: Take from several, or take enough that someone catastrophically broken can function through the next hours.
tree.cannot: The load is cumulative and does not clear on its own. A Threnodist who takes too much becomes someone who needs a Threnodist.

tree.name: Borne Grief
tree.grants: Carry a person's whole weight for a time — a parent at a graveside, a commander after a rout — so they can do the thing that must be done today.
tree.cannot: ⚠ YOU ARE NOW THE ONE CARRYING IT and you may be carrying it long after they have recovered. This is the craft that ends Threnodists, and every one of them knows it and does it anyway.
